_comment: Rank-keyed expectations for genes that exist outside the vertebrate 13+2+22 set.
One machine-readable asset rather than class checks scattered through the QC code.
Each rule names the rank it is keyed on (phylum/class/order), the taxon value,
the gene, and whether a missing gene BLOCKS the annotation or is merely ADVISORY.
Matching is case-insensitive and the first matching rule at the most specific rank
wins. A sample whose taxonomy does not populate that rank simply matches no rule:
in NOVA_260909_LA most invertebrates have a blank order, so an order-keyed rule is
inert for them, which is exactly why nothing here is load-bearing on its own.
The rule that actually catches the NOVA_260909_LA losses is not in this file at
all: 'MITOS called it and conversion lost it is always an error' is unconditional
and lives in annotation_stats.py. This file only says what SHOULD be there when
Evidence for the counts below: the local curated reference DB, 2026-09.

rules.evidence: Octocorallia carry a mitochondrial mismatch-repair gene: 300/302 local Octocorallia reference records annotate it, 0/335 Hexacorallia do.
As Malacalcyonacea: mtMutS is an octocoral gene, not an anthozoan one. Deliberately NOT keyed on class Anthozoa, which would wrongly fail every hexacoral.
81/87 local poriferan reference records carry ATP9 (58/64 Demospongiae). Common but not universal, so a missing ATP9 is reported, never blocking.
58/64 local Demospongiae reference records carry ATP9.
Glass sponges carry ATP9 in the local reference set; treated as advisory on the same footing as Demospongiae.
